summary: Denise Bernot was a linguist who studied at the École des chartes (ca. 1943–1947) and the École des Langues Orientales (ca. 1947–1950). She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from ca. 1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche studied Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric Monastery, under teachers including Ling Rinpoche and Tenzin Gyatso. He served as principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991).

Dennis A. Johnson specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and held a post at its South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library (attested 2022).

Dennis Genpo Merzel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southern California (ca. 1962–1966) and the USC Rossier School of Education (ca. 1966–1968), and trained under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi (ca. 1972–1995).

Dennis Hirota works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of California, Berkeley and Nagoya University, he served at the Hongwanji International Center (ca. 1974–1993) and as professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (ca. 1993–1997) and Ryukoku University (ca. 1997–2017).

Denzaburo Yoshizawa was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1945–1948) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (ca. 1960–1987) and Iryo Sosei University (ca. 1987–1995).

Derek F. Maher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins, and served as co-director of the Religious Studies Program at East Carolina University (attested 2010).

Dermot Killingley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oxford, Merton College, and SOAS, later teaching at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and serving as Reader at Newcastle University from ca. 1970 to 2000.

Dermott Walsh works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a BA at Trinity College Dublin, an MA at Leiden University, and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2018 under doctoral supervisor William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917) and as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen pursued studies under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khenpo Shenga.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse. He participated in a research project at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.

Dharmananda Damodar Kosambi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University in 1926. He held posts at the University of Calcutta, Harvard University, Gujarat University, and the University of Saint Petersburg.

Dhirendra Mohan Datta worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at the University of Calcutta from ca. 1918 to 1923. He held academic posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held teaching posts at the Open University (attested 2017) and the University of Chester (2019).

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Luo earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016) under doctoral supervisors Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, after studying under MA supervisor James Steele.

Diana L. Eck is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Since ca. 1976, she has held a professorship at Harvard University.

Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. She studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Berlin (PhD), and EPHE (Habilitation), and held research roles at Berlin, Hamburg, and a 2025 professorship in Central Asian history and cultures at Berlin.
